safety_class_disclaimer.not_a_project_published_artefact_reason: This requirement belongs to the fictional reference project this corpus declares in its synthetic_reference profile, not to the foxBMS 2 product. foxBMS 2 published no requirement of any kind with an identifier, and nothing was ever allocated to an ASIL on its behalf. It is the reference project's system-level enforcement obligation, written by this corpus. Its own limitations field says it establishes nothing about the real foxBMS project.
safety_class_disclaimer.misreading_warning: A reader who sees an ASIL_D system requirement that mandates a degraded mode distinct from the safe state, mapped to ISO 26262 Part 4 Clause 7 with status `mapped`, will conclude the product distinguishes a recoverable degradation from a limit violation by design. The design is the reference project's, its own limitations say so, and the distinction rests on FB2-ASM-001 and FB2-ASM-005, declared assumptions about cell chemistry and measurement noise.

derivation_basis.locator: No source of its own. The comparison behaviour it states is at src/app/application/soa/soa.c:81-146 (SOA_CheckVoltages) and the degradation reporting at src/app/engine/diag/cbs/diag_cbs_voltage.c:72-194 (DIAG_ErrorOvervoltage), pinned commit 308028fb13d046ba29b98886895c2e17937b1437. The 2.5V/4.2V limits and the 2-of-100 ms debounce come from FB2-ASM-001 and FB2-ASM-005, declared assumptions of the fictional project.
derivation_basis.what_it_supports: That the pinned source compares against configured limits and reports through a diagnostic, so a degraded/safe distinction is a real subject for a system requirement. It supports nothing about the specific limits, the debounce, the degraded-mode behaviour as a design, or the ASIL.

revision_history.description: Added safety_class_disclaimer, carrying no modification of the statement, the ASIL value, the allocation, the acceptance criteria or any standards mapping. The defect corrected is legibility: this record was already marked `profile: synthetic_reference` and, for the SYRs, already says in its own limitations field that it establishes nothing about the real project - but a reader skimming `artifact_type`, `asil` and `standards_mappings` sees a safety requirement at an ASIL with an ISO 26262 clause and status `mapped`, and reads it as an allocated, conformant safety obligation of the product. It is a requirement of the fictional reference project this corpus declares. derivation_basis names what the derivation actually rests on - for most of these, specific pinned file:line ranges, and for FB2-SAF-FSR-000004, FB2-HW-TSR-000004, FB2-SYS-SYR-000004 and FB2-SYS-SYR-000005, the explicit statement that there is no such source because the subject does not exist - and states what it does not support. No other field of the record was modified.

statement: The item shall compare every monitored cell voltage against the configured maximum and minimum limits, shall require two consecutive violations within 100 ms before classifying a violation, and shall move to its degraded mode rather than to the safe state when a measurement channel's disagreement is explainable by a degradation within the declared plausibility envelope, escalating to the safe state only when the degradation removes the reference the item needs.
rationale: The first half of this requirement restates the enforcement the safety goal needs. The second half is new at system level and is the boundary the stakeholder need FB2-SYS-NED-000002 depends on: the difference between a degraded item that stays usable and an item that disconnects on the first channel disagreement. Neither the existing SOA software requirement nor the plausibility requirement states that boundary, because in both cases the boundary is a question about the integrated item's behaviour rather than about one module's algorithm. The corpus records no numerical value for the degraded-to-fault boundary and this requirement deliberately does not invent one; it requires the boundary to exist and to be declared, which is what makes its absence visible.

acceptance_criteria.measure: Consecutive violations required within the window
Time from a value being available to its classification being available
Moderate channel disagreement producing a degraded state rather than a safe state
Total loss of the reference channel producing the safe state
Numerical value or named rule separating degraded from fault

safety_allocation.mitigation: Debounce, plausibility and redundancy comparison, with the degraded-mode capability described in the functional safety concept

limitations: Synthetic. This requirement describes a hypothetical programme and establishes nothing about the real foxBMS project.

System-level only. It does not carry the hardware or software detail, which lives in FB2-HW-TSR-* and FB2-SW-SWR-*. Where this record and those records disagree, neither is silently preferred and the disagreement is raised as a finding.
Not verified against the product. Every measure that touches its allocated requirements is a synthetic fixture or a blocked record; see the FB2-VER-EXE-* set.
